cardinal_sin_flags.fix: Soften to 'the reported allegation concerned approval of payment claims, not the tender award itself.'

cardinal_sin_flags.fix: Remove or soften to 'payment-claim approval can become a corruption choke point when internal controls are weak.'

omitted_facts: Scoop (14 Apr 2026) named the body as Stadium Corporation Malaysia (Perbadanan Stadium Malaysia, PSM), a statutory body under the Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS); Bernama and The Star/Bernama did NOT name the body.
KBS official agency-head page listed Iliyas Bin Jamil as CEO of PSM, but does not itself link him to the MACC case.
Scoop stated the case was investigated under MACC Act 2009 Section 17A (corporate liability) — analysis prudently avoids this citation unless verified.
A separate MACC investigation into alleged irregularities in National Stadium Bukit Jalil upgrade works was reported 29 May 2026 — related by institution/location but not proven the same case.
source_assessment: Relies on ~6 Malaysian media reports, several reproducing Bernama's MACC-source report. Adequate for narrow arrest/remand facts, weak for diversity (essentially one institutional channel). No direct MACC press release, court doc, charge sheet, procurement doc, or AGC charging confirmation.
overall_assessment: Mostly reliable on core reported facts. Main weaknesses are the analytical overlay: 'not for rigging a contract' and 'single-signatory payment certification' are stronger than verified sources support; time-qualify 'not charged'; avoid implying a charge exists. With those changes, publication-safe while preserving process-not-people framing.
